plain_description.what: Tests a new way to certify a 2-way split: find the split axis on one random half of the items and test for two bumps on the other half. It is run on artificial data with planted splits of known size, on structureless data, and on stretched-but-single-bump data. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: The current certificate needs a planted split of about delta 10 before it fires; this asks whether a simple held-out bimodality test does better without being fooled by stretched clouds.
plain_description.information: Shows whether choosing the split on one half and testing for two bumps on the other half detects real planted 2-way structure without being fooled by stretched single-bump clouds. Result: done. It detected all 60 planted splits at a size the existing site test missed (0 of 30), flagged none of 300 null clouds and none of 70 stretched controls, and caught all 15 known merged pairs. This holds for 3 MMLU-Pro categories on one tree member; the precision claim rests on an assumed dependence (DEFF 1.5) that could not be measured at this size.
